items.summary: Standard & Poor's placed Nvidia on downgrade watch while warning its board may be compromised by the long tenure of certain members and governance practices that have not kept pace with the company's rapid growth. The ratings agency said it could downgrade Nvidia within 90 days, but expects any potential downgrade to be limited to one notch unless investigations or other disclosures harm the company's reputation or future business prospects. This move comes amid a turbulent leadership period: Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang on Monday after he resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs with direct reports and Alice Huang, alleged by US intelligence to be Beijing's spy, though Reuters reported Wednesday that the Justice Department did not conduct a formal investigation before President Trump pushed for his return. Investors were largely unruffled by S&P's action even as Nvidia shares fell 38% since October 6; Nvidia closed down nearly 4% on Wednesday after the Nasdaq 100 index briefly flirted with a 20% decline from its recent high. The five-year credit default swap spread for Nvidia was little changed despite rising insurance costs against tech defaults, and Nvidia retains an 'AA' rating indicating very strong capacity to meet financial commitments.
items.title: S&P Puts Nvidia on Downgrade Watch, Citing Possible Board Compromise

items.summary: A November 26, 2026 article explains that despite years of tightening US restrictions on advanced semiconductors to China—beginning with the October 2022 sweeping rules, a January 2025 global license requirement, and further tightening in May 2025—the Trump administration's failure to enforce those measures left gaps that let Chinese companies rent computing power remotely from data centers such as Singapore. The House Foreign Affairs Committee released licensing data showing the Trump administration approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026. To close these gaps, last week the Trump administration issued a new regulation adding license requirements to five countries including Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand—Southeast Asian nations viewed as transshipment points—and clamped down on sales to non-US data centers supplying high volumes of computing power to Chinese-headquartered firms; it also formally rescinded and replaced an earlier rule. The article traces how China nonetheless gained access through the Megaspeed case: for over two years authorities investigated whether Megaspeed diverted chips to China, but license-free purchases by companies in countries including Singapore were permitted until last week's new rule cut off that practice. Last week Megaspeed was added to a US trade blacklist along with its Thai and Malaysian subsidiaries—essentially blocking shipments—and Nvidia said it had already cut off sales to Megaspeed in June 2025; the H200 chip, which Trump allowed Nvidia to ship to China about a year ago amid criticism that it could help jumpstart China's military modernization, was among those involved. The diversion angle is underscored by March charges against three people associated with Super Micro Computer for diverting about $2.5 billion of US technology into China, including AI servers packed with Nvidia chips; critics note Huang's claim that there is no evidence of smuggling is skeptical because the Grace Blackwell platform weighs nearly 1.8 metric tons and would be routed through third countries rather than smuggled in backpacks. In response to this scandal, Nvidia confirmed in December 2025 it has built location verification technology indicating which country its chips operate in—offered as a software option—but opposed proposed legislation requiring such reporting; the Chip Security Act is among export control bills gaining momentum and may be included in next month's National Defense Authorization Act.
items.title: New US export rule and Megaspeed blacklist explain how China accessed Nvidia AI chips

items.summary: A CBS News investigation found that Nvidia is supplying some of its most advanced AI chips to US-based companies with Chinese ownership, raising questions about whether American export restrictions are effectively keeping sensitive technology out of China. The report identified at least two California firms on Nvidia's preferred partner lists: RiCloud AI Inc., whose parent Yuxing InfoTech Investment Holdings Ltd is headquartered in Shenzhen and listed on the Hong Kong exchange; its chief executive Cong Yu holds a degree from a military-run university, while chairman Li Qiang previously led Global Switch Holdings. Another firm, Aivres (formerly Inspur), changed its name after Chinese firms belonging to the parent's group were added to a US federal blacklist in March 2023. Some of these US-based firms have leased or sold advanced chips to companies in Southeast Asia; for example, RiCloud signed a $120 million agreement this year (q4) to lease 300 Nvidia B300 servers (q5) to Agencia Comercial Spirits, and Aivres exported at least $5.6 billion worth of advanced technology to Southeast Asia between April 2024 (d8) and February 2026 (d9), about $3 billion (q10) of which involved computers with Nvidia's Blackwell chips supplied to Malaysia-based Megaspeed and Aolani, where Alice Huang was a senior executive. The investigation also noted that in November last year Nvidia changed its sales reporting from billing location to customer headquarters, revealing an additional $7.9 billion (q14) in 2024 sales billed to China-headquartered companies; under the new method US customers accounted for 69% of sales while China accounted for 9%. CBS News said these complex ownership structures and multiple layers of transactions have made it difficult to establish where chips ultimately end up.
items.title: Nvidia's China Link

items.summary: A CBS News investigation found that Nvidia is selling some of its most advanced artificial intelligence chips to at least two U.S.-based companies controlled by Chinese-owned firms, raising concerns about efforts to keep sensitive technology out of rival countries. One examined company, RiCloud AI in San Jose, California, is listed as an Nvidia 'preferred partner' and was granted that status by December 2025; its parent firm Yuxing InfoTech Investment Holdings Limited is headquartered in Shenzhen, China, and its chief executive Cong Yu holds a degree from the People's Liberation Army Command College. Another company, Aivres (formerly Inspur), manufactures data center servers containing Nvidia chips and exported at least USD 5.6 billion worth of advanced technology to Southeast Asia between April 2024 and February 2026 per a New York Times analysis of trade records; around USD 3 billion of those exports involved computers with Nvidia's China-restricted Blackwell chips, supplied to Malaysian firms Megaspeed and Aolani that provide cloud AI services to Chinese companies Alibaba and ByteDance. The report places these findings alongside the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO amid a separate investigation into Singapore-based Megaspeed over allegations it circumvented export restrictions for China, noting that national security experts view such cases as part of a broader issue given Nvidia's nearly USD 20 billion in sales to China last year. C4ADS analyst Mishel Kondi called the findings 'a wake-up call' about accountability and enforcement.
items.title: Nvidia AI Chips Reach Chinese-Linked Firms, Raising US Security Concerns

items.summary: The National EPA has granted environmental approval for the Western Downs Digital Park, an Anthropic-backed $32 billion data centre in Queensland that it found unlikely to have a significant impact on matters of national environmental significance. The decision came after just two months — far faster than the more than three-year average federal approvals time in Queensland reported by the Queensland Productivity Commission this week — and a government spokesperson said it was made quickly because of the project's thoughtful design and site selection, with no public comments during the referral submission phase. Federal approval does not end the process; the development remains subject to council and state approval.
items.title: Australia's Federal Government Grants Environmental Approval to Anthropic-Backed Data Centre

items.summary: The US Trade Representative proposed additional tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, with the base rate set at 17%, if a bilateral trade deal is not signed. The Trump administration's Section 301 investigation against 16 countries for alleged structural excess capacity led it to propose levies ranging from 15-20% across 14 offending nations, placing developed economies at the lower end and China, Vietnam, and Singapore near the top of that band. India falls in the 18% bracket but retains a one-percentage-point comparative advantage if an agreement finalized last February is signed before final hearings conclude; those hearings are scheduled for January 25, 2027, with fresh levies likely to take effect next February. The proposed tariffs exempt two major Indian exports—pharmaceuticals and mobile phones. India's government rejected the structural excess capacity charges on Wednesday and said it would work toward an early conclusion of a bilateral trade agreement.
items.title: Trump Proposes New Tariffs on 14 Nations; India Faces Additional 17%

items.summary: Eleven days after a leadership transition began, NVIDIA's board reinstated Jensen Huang to the CEO position on November 23. The change reportedly followed input from the US government with President Donald Trump at its center, transforming what might otherwise have been a routine leadership shift into an unusual corporate episode. This development raises questions about whether NVIDIA's board exercised independent judgment or whether Washington's strategic interests influenced the reversal of the transition. It also highlights the extent to which governments can influence decisions made by private companies when such firms become critical to national technological and economic priorities.
items.title: NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After 11-Day Leadership Transition, Raising Questions About Government Influence

items.summary: New US export controls on advanced AI chips have stalled billions of dollars in data centre deals tied to Chinese firms ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent. The curbs require companies in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil to obtain a government licence before purchasing advanced AI chips from American manufacturers, while globally existing data centres that lease significant compute to Chinese firms must secure a separate licence within a 90-day window. As a result, lenders have halted or slowed financing for several near-completion deals: some are delaying the US$6.6 billion (S$8.51 billion) loan sought by Bain Capital's Bridge Data Centres over its Malaysian facilities used by ByteDance; one bank passed on a fully underwritten US$372 million loan for Partners Group-backed Digital Halo, which services Alibaba and other customers in Malaysia; banks are reassessing a US$480 million loan for Singapore-based neocloud Aolani, also backed partly by ByteDance; and at least one fund declined to participate in a US$300 million loan to GMI Cloud for chips powering a Thai data centre used by Tencent. Lenders including Citigroup and Standard Chartered, along with Singapore's major banks, have launched sweeping reviews of their data centre clients, while some are seeking to reduce exposure through secondary loan sales—for example, United Overseas Bank is pursuing a significant risk transfer deal of around US$1 billion tied to data centre loans, though progress has slowed amid the news. The chill extends beyond debt financing: DayOne Data Centers, whose largest customer is ByteDance, has put plans for a US public listing on hold, and a consortium involving BlackRock is considering lowering its offer for a portfolio of Asia Pacific data centres. According to Bloomberg's compiled data, loans to data centre companies in the Asia-Pacific region have risen from virtually zero to more than US$49 billion since 2023. Ben Kostrzewa, an international trade lawyer at Hogan Lovells Cadwalader, said the restrictions could be a beneficial pause for reviewing projects given how frothy the market has been; he added that it will slow but not stop data centre construction or the broader market.
items.title: AI Chip Curbs Halt Billions in Asia Data Centre Loans

items.summary: OpenAI has begun rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience to a small group of Pro subscribers, merging the usage limits for conversational and work-focused features into a single meter across ChatGPT. Product lead Thibault 'Tibo' Sottiaux announced the rollout on X Tuesday, following an earlier email announcement from OpenAI. An OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch that while most users are not expected to face more frequent usage resets, a small fraction of its heaviest users may hit their limits sooner amid criticism from subscribers who fear reduced access to advanced reasoning models for the same subscription fees. Under the new system, conversations using the Instant model will remain unlimited and will not count toward the shared allowance, and users can continue using Instant after exhausting their usage limits; OpenAI also said it would keep working to improve efficiency so subscribers get more from their plans. The company plans to extend shared usage limits more broadly in December per its support page. Rival Anthropic made a similar move earlier this year by combining Claude with its work-focused Cowork under one interface in September. These changes come as AI companies face mounting infrastructure costs and growing demand for increasingly capable models, which is putting pressure on computing resources, while the unified interface could also make chatbots simpler to use by letting users switch between chats and more complex tasks without changing tabs.
items.title: OpenAI Rolls Out Unified ChatGPT Usage Meter; Heaviest Users May Hit Limits Sooner

items.summary: In a Full Story podcast episode, Jonathan Yerushalmy and Reged Ahmad examine what many are describing as an extraordinary intervention by President Donald Trump before Nvidia decided to reinstate Jensen Huang as its CEO. The hosts analyze how the US president is taking credit for Nvidia's move, why it has been characterized as unprecedented, and what might have motivated him to become involved in the decision.
items.title: Trump Claims Credit for Nvidia's Decision to Reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO

items.summary: In the Hyderabad Cricket Association's 'A' Division Tournament Eliminator, Balaaji defeated Gemini Friends by five wickets as Shubham Sharma's unbeaten 56 powered them to a chase of 205 in just 32 overs. Earlier bowled out for 204 all out in 40.3 overs (Mohd Rizwan 31, Abdul Ela Al Qureshi 33, Aryan Cariappa 47), Gemini Friends were restricted by Balaaji's Paraj Raj (49), H K Simha (33), Shubham Sharma (56 n.o) and K Sri Harsha (33 n.o). In the Vijay Merchant Trophy third-round opening day at Shivamogga, Hyderabad bowled out Chandigarh for 204 in 86.1 overs as Aaryan Rath and Anirudh Naik claimed three wickets apiece off 36 runs each; Rayaan top-scored with 61 while Tejaspreet Singh made 32 and Shivansh Choudhary added 30, leaving Hyderabad at 2 for no loss in one over by close of play. In the HCA 'B' Division quarterfinal, Narra Chandra's brilliant 131 off 133 balls (13 fours, five sixes) helped Warangal District post 319/7 to beat Vijay Hanuman by 73 runs as A. Nagaraju took 5/51; Vijay Hanuman scored 246 in 44 overs with C Lehar Vishal (32), Sai Raj (63) and B Sairam Vasishta (36). The 'C' Division saw Yashmith Reddy G top-score with 130 for Satyam Colts, who beat Mahbub College by chasing 206/7 in 45 overs after the visitors were bowled out for 189; Raju Cricket Centre chased down Sri Shyam's 186 to win (Mahidhar K unbeaten on 119). Reliance posted 260 all out as Tanush Rathore took 6/11 in a crushing victory over Ranga Reddy District, who were bowled out for just 67. The HCA Senior & Under-19 Women's selection matches featured Team E beating Team B by three wickets (Team B posted 269 all out), and Team F edging Team A after both reached 245 in the chase of a level total.
items.title: Balaaji Eliminate Gemini Friends; Chandra and Nagaraju Stand Out in Local Cricket

visual.alt: Bar chart. Narra Chandra 131; Yashmith Reddy G 61; Rayaan (Chandigarh) 30.

items.summary: Hours after President Donald Trump announced new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including the European Union, China, Japan, South Korea, Singapore and several Southeast Asian economies, Vietnam said it was working with Washington to conclude a trade agreement as soon as possible. The US is Vietnam's largest export market, though its trade deficit with Vietnam is the largest of any partner relationship. Under the USTR proposal, Vietnamese goods would face a capped tariff rate of 20 per cent if an agreement is reached, or up to 35 per cent if negotiations fail; Trump's administration proposed headline rates between 20 and 40 per cent across its new duties. Vietnam said it will participate fully in the next stages of the investigation, including registering for and attending a public hearing scheduled after January 25. Meanwhile, Taiwan expressed confidence that Washington would maintain the previously agreed 15 per cent tariff rate, citing communications with the US. Preferential arrangements secured through an investment cooperation memorandum signed in January and an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade signed in February have given semiconductors and other technology products—accounting for more than 70 per cent of Taiwan's exports to the US—preferential treatment.
items.title: Asian Economies Respond to Trump's New Tariffs

items.summary: On Nov 25, the Nasdaq Composite fell 154.10 points (0.65%) to close at 23,579.44 and the S&P 500 lost 18.01 points (0.25%) to end at 7,183.08, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 155.20 points (0.31%) to 50,173.90. Both indexes retreated amid a tech sell-off but finished well off their day's lows as bargain hunters stepped in ahead of Thanksgiving; the Nasdaq had been more than 4% lower earlier in the session before recovering.
items.title: Nasdaq and S&P 500 End Down but Well Off Lows as Investors Buy the Dip

items.summary: On November 25, 2026, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the Federal Reserve Board, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency announced that the dollar threshold exempting smaller higher-priced mortgage loans from special appraisal requirements will rise to $35,500 in 2027. The new figure increases from $34,200 and takes effect January 1, 2027. Under Dodd-Frank Act rules added to the Truth in Lending Act, creditors must obtain a written appraisal based on an interior physical visit before making such loans, but this requirement does not apply to loans at or below the threshold amount. The agencies set the $35,500 figure using CPI-W data: it reflects the 3.9 percent annual percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers as of June 1, 2026.
items.title: CFPB, Federal Reserve and OCC Raise Higher-Priced Mortgage Appraisal Exemption Threshold to $35,500 for 2027

items.summary: On November 25, 2026, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and the Federal Reserve Board announced the dollar thresholds used to determine whether consumer credit transactions in 2027 are subject to protections under Regulation Z (Truth in Lending) and Regulation M (Consumer Leasing). By law, the agencies must adjust these thresholds annually based on the annual percentage increase in CPI-W. Based on a 3.9 percent annual percentage increase in CPI-W as of June 1, 2026, the regulations will generally apply to consumer credit transactions and leases of $76,300 or less in 2027. However, private education loans and loans secured by real property such as mortgages are subject to Regulation Z regardless of loan amount.
items.title: CFPB and Federal Reserve Set Consumer Credit Thresholds for 2027

items.summary: The Trump administration announced proposed additional tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 against 14 trading partners, with rates ranging from 15% to 35%, according to US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. The measures target what Washington describes as structural excess manufacturing capacity and come after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's use of emergency powers in February, paving the way for a 10% baseline tariff (q8). China faces up to 20% on specified goods, which could raise its total burden to 45% when combined with existing duties (q11, q12), while Vietnam is set at 35%, reducible to 20% if negotiations conclude (q17, q18). India's rate would reach 25%, or fall to 17% if a trade deal is reached; Washington had previously lowered most Indian tariffs from 50% to 18% under an August 2025 framework agreement that has not yet been finalized (q4, q3, q6, d7). The administration plans public hearings on January 25 and expects the duties to take effect no earlier than February or March. Goldman Sachs estimates implementation would raise the overall effective US tariff rate from 7.8% to 9.2%, with only a small incremental impact on inflation.
items.title: US Proposes Section 301 Tariffs on 14 Countries

items.summary: Investors facing a sharp surge in volatility are moving toward safe havens as the collapse in the AI trade has been compounded by fresh risks from new U.S. tariffs. On Wednesday, the United States proposed country-specific tariffs on goods from 14 major trading partners—including India, Japan, and the European Union—while applying an additional 20% tariff on imports from China (per q1:
items.title: Tariff Mayhem and Tech Pain Push Volatility-Weary Investors to Safe Havens

items.summary: US President Donald Trump pushed for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO of Nvidia because of his support for US open-weight models, which offer an alternative to Chinese versions. However, Huang's return could also spur Beijing to accelerate its own efforts to build homegrown chips. Tech executives have emphasized how damaging a leadership vacuum at Nvidia would have been for the sector, given Huang's role as both industry cheerleader and central banker, along with Nvidia's promotion of the computing platforms developers use to train and run open models. One AI startup founder noted that the open-source world is bigger than one individual, even if that person is Jensen Huang. The article suggests that if a newly emboldened Washington intensifies scrutiny of chip sales to China and curbs Beijing's access to advanced computing power, it could slow down China's AI labs as well as Western companies' efforts to stay ahead.
items.title: Huang's Return to Nvidia Complicates the Open-Source Model Race

items.summary: Despite midterm voters punishing Republicans over an economy and inflation that many attributed to tariffs, the Trump administration announced a new round of tariffs on Wednesday targeting goods from 14 major trading partners, including China, Japan, and the European Union. This move reflects both President Donald Trump's long-held belief in tariffs and a shifting political reality: with Democrats expected to control Congress for the final two years of his presidency, tariffs have become one of the most significant economic tools available to him without requiring legislative approval.
items.title: Trump Expands Tariffs Despite Recent Voter Backlash

items.summary: Energy Minister Chris Bowen told the House that Australia's average coal-fired power stations are about 40 years old and increasingly unreliable, declaring they 'must be replaced' after experiencing at least one breakdown every day for three consecutive years. He linked these outages to skyrocketing energy prices. In response to Labor's climate statement, Coalition spokesman Dan Tehan said the bills were causing 'real pain,' especially ahead of Christmas, noting that while wholesale national market prices fell 27% in the year to September (q1), retail energy prices rose 25% in the year to October as rebates expired. Bowen defended Australia's Cop31 leadership, saying negotiators reached agreement on 44 of 60 substantive items and many countries signed a '35 by 35' pledge to raise electricity's share of global energy consumption to 35% by 2035 (q7–q13). He said Australia is forecast to cut emissions by 42% on 2005 levels by 2030, just under its 43% target (q14), with annual emissions already 25.3% below 2005 levels and a fall of 6.2m tonnes in the year to June (q19–q23). Bowen also said rooftop solar installation was 45% higher than in the same period in 2025, that more solar panels now exist on rooftops than backyard swimming pools, and that the home batteries program has helped install over 622,000 batteries (17.35GWh). Separately, new One Nation senator Leah Blyth said she did not 'feel safe' in the Liberal party before her defection.
items.title: Australian energy minister says ageing coal stations must be replaced as emissions fall short of target

items.summary: According to the Reserve Bank of India's half-yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves for April-September 2026, RBI shifted 60.1 tonnes (q1) of gold from overseas vaults to domestic storage over that period, raising its share held in India to 84 per cent (q3). Total gold reserves remained almost unchanged at 880.5 tonnes (q4), with domestic holdings rising to 740.1 tonnes (q6) from 575.8 tonnes (q7) recorded in September 2025 (d8), while overseas holdings fell to 140.4 tonnes (q9) from 290.4 tonnes (q10). The RBI attributed the shift to central banks' growing preference for domestic gold custody, and noted that a further 60.1-tonne transfer occurred in the preceding six months ending March 2026 (d11, q12). Separately, India's total forex reserves rose to $737.8 billion (q13) from $691.1 billion (q14) in March after peaking at $751.8 billion (q15) in August; foreign currency assets increased to $608.3 billion (q16), while gold reserves fell to $106.1 billion (q17). Gold's share of forex reserves declined to 14.4 per cent (q18) from 16.7 per cent (q19), reflecting a 9 per cent fall in international gold prices and a 4 per cent appreciation in the US Dollar Index during the half-year (q20, q21). At September-end, 87.1 per cent (q22) of foreign currency assets were held in overseas securities, with 7 per cent (q23) in deposits with commercial banks and 5.9 per cent (q24) with other central banks and the BIS. RBI's latest gold purchase was just over 0.1 tonnes in January 2026, following a four-month pause.
items.title: RBI Moved 60.1 Tonnes of Gold Overseas to Domestic Storage in Six Months

visual.alt: Bar chart. Domestic storage 740.1 tonne; Overseas holdings (Bank of England and BIS) 140.4 tonne.

items.summary: Hours after the Trump administration announced new tariffs on 14 trading partners to address excess factory capacity, Vietnam's Ministry of Industry and Trade said it is working with the United States to complete a trade deal as soon as possible. In a statement released Nov. 26 in Hanoi, the ministry said it would coordinate with relevant U.S. agencies to fully participate in the next stages of the USTR's investigation process, including registering for and attending public hearings, presenting views, and responding to questions from U.S. officials.
items.title: Vietnam Says It Is Working With U.S. To Complete Trade Deal

items.summary: The Trump administration proposes a dual-rate tariff framework that would impose duties of up to 25% on Indian exports without a bilateral trade agreement, compared with 17% if one is finalized (q7, q8). The eight-percentage-point differential creates a financial incentive for New Delhi to conclude negotiations. On an illustrative shipment valued at $100,000, the 25% rate would translate into duties of $25,000 versus $17,000 under the deal rate (q12-q15). India's proposed 17% deal rate offers only a marginal headline advantage over competing manufacturing economies: Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand face 18%, while Vietnam and China face 20% (q6, q16-q18), with China's rate imposed alongside existing 2018 Section 301 tariffs (d19, q20). The USTR proposed these tariffs targeting 14 economies following investigations launched in March 2026 (q10, d11). According to the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), the differential is designed to encourage India to conclude an agreement, though GTRI warns that tariff relief may come at the cost of unilateral trade concessions and notes a potential threat of Graham tariffs of up to 100% remains additional uncertainty (q5, q9, q21). Washington's investigation flagged excess capacity or export surpluses across seven Indian manufacturing sectors including solar modules, steel, textiles, petrochemicals and automotive products.
items.title: Trump's Tariff Differential Pressures India to Finalize Trade Deal

items.summary: Poonawalla Fincorp shares rose about 25% over three weeks, with management attributing the rally to improving lending yields. During the September quarter, the yield on fresh disbursements was more than 200 basis points higher than the portfolio yield (q1), and the company's overall portfolio yield climbed 45 basis points sequentially to 14.1% in that period (q2, q3). Management says these higher-yielding loans are gradually entering the existing book, which is expected to push yields up further and support margin expansion. Motilal Oswal Financial Services projects net interest margin rising from 7% in FY26 to 7.7% in FY27 and 7.9% in FY28 (q6, q7, q8), citing the portfolio yield improvement along with favorable product mix and pricing flexibility; it has retained its 'Buy' rating on the stock with a price target of ₹600 versus Wednesday's closing price of ₹510, implying roughly 19% upside (q9, q10, q11). Growth is being driven by digital personal loans, gold loans, consumer durable financing and education loans, which together accounted for 28% of total disbursements in the September quarter (q13), while a separate Wealthy-Deloitte survey found that 62% of distributors reported growth despite rising redemptions (q12).
items.title: Poonawalla Fincorp Shares Rally as Improving Lending Yields Drive Margin Expansion Outlook

items.summary: Investors in Anthropic's recent IPO face a risk that cheaper AI models will erode the company's revenue, even as its shareholders hoped Claude would keep commanding premium prices. The article centers on this tension: while each unit of AI work is getting dramatically less expensive, businesses are still paying top rates for the most capable models—yet Anthropic must sell far more volume to grow because it has locked in multiyear computing commitments that cannot be cut easily.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO Bets on Premium Pricing Despite Falling AI Token Costs

items.summary: The article's title asserts a $900 billion bet by Anthropic on customer loyalty, but the supporting evidence does not address this figure. Instead it illustrates how cheap alternatives are undercutting Claude: San Diego operations manager Stu Clott switched from Anthropic's model to DeepSeek after an hour of coding cost about $10 with Claude versus less than 50 cents with DeepSeek (q1 and q2), leaving him paying
items.title: Anthropic is betting $900 billion that customers won't switch to cheaper AI

items.summary: A US court found Chinese tech giant Huawei guilty of fraud, finding it responsible for 10 out of 12 counts while not convicting it of the most serious charge, racketeering. The verdict elicited an angry reaction from Beijing and deepens tensions between the two countries amid mounting trade friction: the US is clamping down on chip sales to China and reportedly weighing new tariffs on the world's second-biggest economy. Western firms have long accused Huawei of stealing intellectual property, while Western capitals accuse China of unfairly supporting its domestic firms to outcompete overseas rivals.
items.title: US Court Finds Huawei Guilty of Fraud on 10 of 12 Counts

items.summary: In an article titled 'A commitment to strengthen our Constitution,' India's Prime Minister reflects on November 26, 1949, when the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution and marks it as Constitution Day. The writer frames the government's efforts over more than a decade since that decision to deepen public connection with the document—especially among youth—as a way of strengthening it. Citing a recent World Bank report, the article states that nearly 50 crore Indians have moved out of poverty (q2). It attributes constitutional progress to specific schemes and reforms: PM Awas Yojana for housing, Ujjwala Yojana for clean cooking fuel, Ayushman Bharat for healthcare access, MUDRA and PM-SVANidhi for collateral-free credit, digital platforms like UPI for inclusivity; the 101st Amendment (GST), the 102nd Amendment granting constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes, and the 103rd Amendment providing reservation to Economically Weaker Sections. The writer also notes that for the first time since 1950, an updated version of the Constitution is available in all 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule (q7), while India continued until Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita to be governed by a colonial penal code dating back to the 1860s (q9). Turning to concerns about constitutional erosion, the article attributes historical misuse to specific events and actors: it describes this year as marking 75 years since the First Amendment of 1951 (d10), when an unelected government restricted fundamental freedoms before India's first general election; 50 years since the 42nd Amendment at Emergency, which curtailed judicial review; repeated misuse of Article 356 to dismiss elected state governments—attributing a record of imposing it almost a hundred times (q14) to one party and a half-century score to one former PM—and urges young people to study the 38th and 39th Amendments. It also states that Articles 370 and 35A prevented full constitutional implementation in Jammu & Kashmir for over 70 years, corrected only in 2019 (d17). The writer credits this year's elimination of Naxalism with enabling the poorest to exercise their rights without fear. Finally, attributing obstructionism to 'the biggest party in the opposition,' the article alleges that party blocked a bill giving women adequate representation in legislative bodies and sought to reduce OBC reservation while adding Muslim reservations—actions the writer says Ambedkar opposed—and frames these as failures of constitutional duty ahead of Viksit Bharat by 2047 (d18).
items.title: India's PM Frames Constitution Day as a Commitment to Strengthen the Nation's Founding Document

items.summary: In an episode of AI Engineer CODE sponsored by Jira by Atlassian, Thariq Shihipar discusses how coding agents can make software cheap enough to produce in volume while still allowing designers time to refine individual pieces. He describes building a fighting game where he edits rock sizes and immediately tests throws, plus a Mac Dock that switched modes so he could notice when he got distracted. The episode covers what surprised him about agents, the concept of a /human folder, software as craft, decision models that choose from designer-defined actions, who decides which experiments deserve compute resources, personal software, adoption patterns, and autoresearch. Shihipar announced his move to OpenAI after the recording was completed.
items.title: Thariq Shihipar Discusses Coding Agents and His Move to OpenAI

items.summary: Hours after the Trump administration announced fresh tariffs on India, New Delhi rejected Washington's allegations that Indian industrial and trade policies create excess manufacturing capacity, insisting it has no surplus production in any sector and that disputes be resolved through bilateral negotiations. The response came amid a Section 301 investigation into alleged structural excess capacity across several economies, including India; the USTR proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian imports (q1, q2), with a provision to cap the rate at 17 per cent if the two countries finalize a trade agreement (q3, q4). The government said it had taken note of the USTR's Notice of Determination and Request for Comments, which is under examination. Section 301 of the US Trade Act of 1974 allows Washington to investigate foreign practices deemed unfair and impose retaliatory tariffs; this investigation covers manufacturing sectors across 14 economies (q5–d8, q9). The USTR cited five alleged Indian practices—industrial plans to expand manufacturing, inadequate labour protections, financial repression policies, sustained market access barriers, and failure to address global excess capacity—and said concerns were especially significant in pharmaceuticals/medical devices, steel, solar energy, and ICT. As a proposed response, the USTR recommended tariffs of up to 25 per cent on all Indian goods (net of existing Section 301 duties), with exemptions for certain products, and considered reducing additional duties to 17 per cent if India reaches a reciprocal trade agreement (q12–q14). Under that proposal, the proposed 17 per cent rate would give India a one-percentage-point advantage over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, which face deal-linked rates of 18 per cent; Vietnam and China would face 20 per cent under their respective arrangements. Trade negotiations remain unfinished: after agreeing on a framework in February 2026 that reduced punitive tariffs from 50 per cent to 18 per cent for most Indian goods, no final agreement has been reached despite several rounds of talks. The investigation was initiated in March as part of a probe covering 16 economies; the US has made determinations against 14—including India—while withholding findings on Mexico and Norway (q15–q17). USTR Jamieson Greer said the proposed duties would generally not be stacked on existing tariffs but rather act as a 'top-up' of only a few additional percentage points in most cases. Public comments must be submitted by January 5, 2027, with hearings scheduled to begin January 25, 2027 (q18–q19).
items.title: India Rejects US Excess-Capacity Allegations as Washington Proposes Tariffs

items.summary: Coastal California is bracing for major flooding as king tides peak during the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday, with water levels potentially reaching over 8ft (2.4 metres) in some areas on Wednesday and Thursday according to the National Weather Service (NWS), surpassing records set just last month. San Diego recorded an 8 ft 11in high tide on Wednesday morning—potentially breaking its prior record of 7.98ft—and Los Angeles saw a tide as high as 8.19, both exceeding recently established benchmarks from late October and early November. These king tides are being intensified by the strongest El Niño weather pattern on record and rising sea levels that make them occur more frequently. Flooding has already been reported in the San Francisco Bay Area, and a pier in northern California collapsed into the ocean Wednesday as high tides and strong waves battered it; beachgoers were warned to stay away from the water's edge due to large, sudden waves that could damage piers and jetties or capsize small vessels. Storm systems are also expected across the Pacific Northwest—including British Columbia—and along the eastern U.S., where a developing Nor'easter is forecast to bring heavy rain (one to four inches coastwide, peaking at four to six inches in coastal North Carolina), strong winds, and major coastal flooding beginning Wednesday in the southeast before moving northward Thursday. Macy's postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade from Thursday to Saturday due to severe weather—the first time this has occurred—while Environment and Climate Change Canada issued a flood warning along British Columbia's coastline urging residents to take immediate action. The stormy conditions on both coasts could disrupt travel for millions, with the American Automobile Association (AAA) predicting 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Tuesday, November 24 and Monday, November 30.
items.title: California Warned of Record King Tides and Storm Flooding Around Thanksgiving

items.summary: Federal Liberal senator for South Australia Leah Blyth announced her defection to Pauline Hanson's One Nation, a move that blindsided former Coalition colleagues and intensified scrutiny of instability within the opposition. In a statement released at the last day of parliament, Blyth said she could no longer in good conscience represent Australians because she did not believe the Coalition was capable of opposing the Albanese government; she praised One Nation as the only party with bold ideas to turn the country around while admitting she was 'not completely across' its policies. She cited the Liberals' support for the controversial defence bases bill, which One Nation also backed, and criticized policy compromises including dropping net zero while remaining in the Paris climate agreement and a digital duty of care measure. Blyth had been named by the Liberal Party to replace Simon Birmingham in 2025 rather than being elected directly, was previously South Australia's state president before being replaced by Alex Antic, and faced re-election on a winnable Senate ticket that she expected to lose; Guardian Australia reported the pair, former allies in the conservative faction, had fallen out. Coalition MPs said they were surprised Blyth did not inform them beforehand, though she told News 24 she was no longer thinking about the Liberal Party and argued Liberals had left many voters disaffected. One Nation's Pauline Hanson welcomed her as an addition to expanding state support, while Nationals leader Matt Canavan called the defection 'disappointing' and self-interested given Blyth's prior support for net zero and hate speech laws; deputy Liberal leader Jane Hume described it as a disappointing decision but noted she was not a major party room contributor.
items.title: Liberal Senator Leah Blyth Defects to One Nation Amid Coalition Fallout

items.summary: Pastor Doug Wilson, a conservative minister based in Moscow, Idaho and described as a Christian nationalist who believes the US should be a theocracy, says he wants the 19th Amendment — which granted women the right to vote — repealed. He favours 'household voting,' where the head of the home votes for the family, under which just 7% of votes in his church polity are cast by women; when challenged he admitted it gives men outsized influence. Wilson co-founded the Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches (CREC), which has around 150 churches in the US compared with roughly 350,000 other Christian congregations there and more than 30 internationally, including in Poland, Japan and Brazil. He says his views have gained support partly through his connection to Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, a 'proud member' of an affiliated church who called Wilson's mentorship valuable at a joint event where Wilson led prayer services. Wilson describes repealing the amendment as low on his priorities but affirms they do think it should happen; he estimates overturning it could take a century or more. Religious studies scholars say his views are misogynistic and extreme, with Professor Julie Ingersoll noting repeal would require two-thirds majorities in both chambers plus ratification by three-quarters of states — making it extremely unlikely — while comparing the effort to the campaign that overturned Roe v Wade in 2022; Associate Professor Kelly Marino says such backlash tends to follow periods of feminist and liberal gains. Younger pastors Dale Partridge, who said his group would repeal the amendment within ten years and has around 900k social media followers, and Joel Webbon, whose New Christian Right YouTube channel has more than 190k subscribers, have pushed for removing women's vote, though Wilson calls them disruptors. Canon Dana Colley Corsello of the Washington National Cathedral rejects Wilson's biblical interpretation as having no precedent.
items.title: US Pastor Doug Wilson Wants the 19th Amendment Repealed

items.summary: Indian equities rose to fresh fiscal-year-2027 highs on a day when Asian markets fell sharply, with the Sensex up 1.82% (1,502 points) to close at 83,938 and the Nifty up 1.85% (469.6 points) to end at 25,819.25 — both their highest levels since February. The rebound followed profit booking on Monday when the Sensex fell 1.77% and the Nifty dropped 1.75%. ICICI Bank (+3.44%), HDFC Bank (+3.2%) and Reliance Industries (+1.5%) were the biggest contributors, together accounting for half of the gains. Foreign funds poured nearly $14.3 billion into Indian equities in November — a monthly record after withdrawing nearly $60 billion over the previous 25 months — which supported the rupee as it rallied 0.7% to 92.23 per dollar, its strongest level since March and the top-performing emerging-market currency this quarter. On NSE data, FPIs were net buyers of ₹4,479.08 crore while domestic institutional investors bought equities worth ₹4,018.72 crore. The gains contrasted with a slump in Asian markets amid concerns over elevated AI valuations and spending plans: Japan's Nikkei fell 2.8%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng declined 1.1% and Shenzhen lost 3.5%. In the US, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq dropped 1.5%, while oil prices slipped on supply concerns.
items.title: Indian Stocks Hit Fresh FY27 Highs While Asian Markets Slumped

items.summary: The United Nations General Assembly agreed on October 29th to extend the graduation deadline for Bangladesh and Nepal by three years, pushing their scheduled exit from the list of least developed countries (LDCs) to November 2029. Both nations qualified for graduation under criteria set in 1971: a Gross National Income per capita threshold of $1,306, a Human Assets Index of 66 or above, and an Economic and Environmental Vulnerability Index of 32 or less (meeting any two of the three across reviews conducted three years apart). The extension reflects their argument that losing LDC status would strip away economic advantages they still depend on. For Bangladesh, roughly 80% of merchandise exports are garments, about 73% of which benefit from LDC-specific trade preferences; once these lapse, exporters could face tariffs averaging 12.5%, potentially costing more than $17.5 billion annually and risking orders shifting to other suppliers. Nepal's situation differs because over two-thirds of its exports go to India under a bilateral treaty that does not depend on LDC status, so EU-related export losses would account for less than 5% of total exports—though it still risks losing preferences in other markets and aid.
items.title: Bangladesh and Nepal Ask to Keep Least Developed Country Status Until November 2029

items.summary: Jenna Bruton is entering North Melbourne's fourth consecutive AFLW grand final this week, seeking a third successive premiership after defeating Melbourne. For the Kangaroo star forward, the milestone carries personal weight: she marked her 100th game in that season's qualifying final against Carlton while wishing her mother and aunt could have been present. Both women died from brain cancer — her mother Suzy was diagnosed in late 2015, prompting Bruton to omit herself from the inaugural 2016 draft so she could become a full-time carer; her partner Jasmine Garner then submitted her belated nomination into the AFLW system. Her aunt Andrea also died of the same cancer just three months before her mother. Bruton was drafted with pick 11 by the Western Bulldogs in 2017 and joined North Melbourne as an expansion player for the 2019 season; her mother passed away a week before the first game of the 2022 season, while Garner noted that without her nomination Bruton would likely still be working on the Trentham potato farm where she grew up. As a three-time premiership player — once with the Bulldogs and twice with North Melbourne — Bruton credits family support through losing both women.
items.title: North Melbourne's Jenna Bruton heads into fourth straight grand final amid family tragedy

items.summary: India faces a chronic shortage of donated human skin that leaves burn patients, especially during the annual Diwali firecracker and diya surge, without life-saving grafts. Sarthak Shinde survived 13% deep burns after doctors transplanted an allograft at Airoli's National Burns Centre; there, 18 of 25 firecracker-related burn patients received skin grafts that year. The shortage is acute in Delhi: Safdarjung hospital recorded 206 burn cases over three Diwali days but could not supply the five extensive-burn patients needing it despite owning one of only three Delhi skin banks, which receives just one to two donors per month; nearby AIIMS faces the same problem, and Faridabad has no bank at all. Mumbai logged 63 firecracker injuries while Delhi recorded nearly 500 this Diwali. Across India's 36 skin banks, only 14 are registered with NOTTO (the central organ-donation body), which coordinated Shinde's graft; those 14 received 440 donations in 2024 and 590 in 2025 per Scroll data, while rough estimates put all 36 banks' annual intake at about 700 to 1,000 donors—levels experts call grossly inadequate. Navi Mumbai's National Burns Institute is the top earner with 207 donations in 2025-26 (up from 157 a decade ago) and 2,430 since its 2009 founding; most other banks manage only 10 to 30 donors yearly. India's first skin bank opened in 1972 at Wadia's Children hospital but shut down for low donations. In 2025 the health ministry announced a centralized registry with live stock data, mandatory registration of banks and transplant centres, and a Rs 15 per square centimetre processing fee—though SeethaRaman of the Association of Plastic Surgeons says there is still no central real-time availability data because government banks' processes are slow. When donated skin is unavailable, patients may turn to synthetic grafts: gangman Prem Kumar's chest and back treatment cost Rs 10 lakh (total care Rs 86 lakh via insurance), versus roughly Rs 15 per square centimetre for human allograft; a small synthetic graft can exceed Rs 40,000. Low awareness and fears of disfigurement further limit donations.
items.title: Diwali Burn Surge Exposes India's Chronic Shortage of Donated Skin

items.summary: In an entry dated 25th November 2026, Scott Aaronson describes a recent development in complexity theory as transformative, comparing the improved resolution into 'the complexity-theoretic universe' to van Leeuwenhoek first examining pondwater and Galileo first observing stars. He characterizes the result not as isolated solutions to individual problems but as opening up an entire new domain of mathematical truth that had previously been only partially visible.
items.title: Scott Aaronson on Complexity Theory Breakthrough

items.summary: A fresh Church-led attempt to bring Nagas and Kukis closer after months of hostility has raised hopes of a possible thaw in Manipur's troubled hill districts. The three-day summit held from November 22 to 24 in Kolkata brought together representatives of several church and civil society organisations, including the Kuki Inpi Manipur, United Naga Council, Kuki Christian Churches Manipur, Kuki Baptist Churches Manipur, Naga Christian Forum Manipur and Naga Peoples' Initiative for Peace Manipur. The latest effort to revive dialogue concluded on Tuesday (November 24) evening with an agreement between the two communities to identify the core issues behind the conflict and address them through sustained discussions. Community leaders from both sides also agreed to hold another round of dialogue before Christmas this year, involving all stakeholders. Participants acknowledged how deeply they had hurt each other and recognised the need to break what it described as the 'chain of fear, hate and violence'. The proposed truce is intended to provide immediate relief to affected families, prevent further loss of life and create a safe environment for discussions on the underlying issues. The FNR also appealed to both communities to stop spreading rumours, hatred and propaganda on social media, which it said were fuelling animosity and polarisation. CoTU spokesperson Ng Lun Kipgen described the move as a positive step towards normalcy and said his organisation supported the efforts of the churches to bring the two communities together. He noted that a similar church-led initiative had been attempted earlier this year but failed after three Kuki church leaders were brutally killed in May, allegedly by members of a Naga armed group. A Kuki intellectual who wished to remain anonymous cautioned that religious solidarity alone cannot resolve the political, territorial and security-related questions underlying the conflict. UNC president Ng Lorho said genuine reconciliation is needed without which there will be no peace. Considering past experience, he acknowledged that the success of the fresh peace initiative will largely depend on the response of militant groups on both sides, but expressed hope they would respect the sentiments of ordinary people who want peace. Kipgen cautioned against viewing the ongoing tensions as a conflict between entire communities and said hostilities involved certain Naga sub-tribes rather than being generalised to the whole population. He added that the state government's willingness to address contentious issues is also crucial, while CoTU's support for the peace initiative would not alter its position on the 72-hour ultimatum for a road blockade. The CoTU has threatened an indefinite shutdown of national highways from November 27 if its five-point charter of demands is not met by Thursday (November 26). Demands include transferring investigation into the October 28 killing of two Kuki-Zo youths at Taphou to the NIA, arresting those responsible, removing Deputy Chief Minister Losii Dikho, transferring police jurisdiction for Taphou village from Senapati district to Kangpokpi, dismantling an alleged NSCN-IM Huthrong Brigade camp at Oklong in Senapati district and withdrawing central and state security forces operating under the Senapati Superintendent of Police from Kangpokpi. Only the demand for an NIA investigation had been met so far. The ongoing Kuki-Naga clashes have claimed at least 71 lives since February 2026, including 38 Kuki-Zo and 33 Naga people according to Manipur police sources.
items.title: Church-led Naga-Kuki peace talks resume in Manipur, but success hinges on armed groups

items.summary: Six months into VD Satheesan's tenure as Chief Minister of Kerala, the Congress party is engulfed in its most acrimonious internal factional conflict since the Karunakaran-Antony era. Satheesan rose to power on an image of transcending Keralam's traditional A and I faction politics after a sweeping United Democratic Front (UDF) victory that ended 10 years out of office, with Congress alone winning 63 seats in the 140-member Assembly against a total UDF result of 102 seats. That post-factional promise is now unraveling as public and personal battles intensify: cabinet meetings reportedly feature confrontations over alleged unilateral decisions by Satheesan; senior ministers and parliamentarians exchange accusations of sabotage and media leaks; rival factions launch coordinated cyberattacks on colleagues; and coalition partners complain about a four-month freeze in alliance meetings. At the center is an emerging realignment, with Oommen Chandy loyalists from the dormant 'A' group converging with Venugopal's organisational camp against Satheesan—though both camps reject conspiracy claims, insisting their grievances are procedural rather than aimed at destabilizing the government. The crisis traces to a leadership decision made in the 10 days between election results and Satheesan's appointment as CM: High Command chose him over AICC general secretary Venugopal despite Venugopal's organisational influence, leaving two powerful centers intact—Satheesan governing while Venugopal retained control of Congress organisation and national leadership. The first flashpoint came in early October when UDF convenor Adoor Prakash attacked Satheesan for unconsulted cabinet-rank appointments to the Kerala Administrative Reforms Commission chairperson and All India Forward Bloc's G Devarajan, exposing that his anti-factional approach lacked a transparent consultative system to replace faction quotas. A second flashpoint emerged when Congress MLA Mathew Kuzhalnadan criticized the government's restrained pursuit of the CMRL pay-off case involving CPI(M) leaders including Pinarayi Vijayan. Tensions exploded on November 18 at six months in office, when ministers confronted Satheesan over unconsulted Kerala Public Service Commission nominations and a dispute with Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph (also KPCC president), with details leaking to television channels and turning an internal discussion into public spectacle. The revival of the A-group by mid-November—projecting Shafi Parambil and PC Vishnunadh as younger faces, floating Benny Behanan for KPCC presidency, and meeting AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge in Delhi—fueled speculation that it was coordinating with Venugopal's camp to pressure Satheesan. The conflict has spilled onto social media through coordinated online attacks, most dramatically when Kasaragod MP Rajmohan Unnithan personally attacked Shafi Parambil over alleged cyberattacks on himself and his son Amal. The infighting is now threatening the wider UDF: the Revolutionary Socialist Party criticized cabinet-rank appointments and absent alliance meetings; Kerala Congress (Joseph) raised concerns over board/corporation appointment delays; and the Indian Union Muslim League lodged a complaint with Rahul Gandhi accusing Venugopal's camp of sidelining it in national INDIA bloc activities, resolving to boycott Venugopal-faction ministers. Observers identify four structural weaknesses: Satheesan dismantled factional politics without building consultative institutions to replace them; he controls government but not the party machinery that rivals retain through KPCC and AICC influence; his reluctance to build a formal faction has prompted supporters to organize defensively, creating the very structure he sought to avoid; and Sunny Joseph's dual role as KPCC president and minister blurs boundaries between government and organisation. Despite escalation, neither camp has submitted a formal complaint—KPCC president Sunny Joseph invited Satheesan to inaugurate a Constitution Protection Day programme on November 26, an extended December meeting could ease tensions, Ramesh Chennithala is mediating, and K Muraleedharan defends the government's completion of its five-year term. The High Command faces a delicate balancing act between Satheesan's electoral mandate and Venugopal's organisational influence, with any intervention risking aggravation rather than resolution.
items.title: Kerala's Congress Faces Its Ugliest Faction War Six Months Into Satheesan Government

items.summary: A suspected cattle smuggler, Mohammad Mustafa of Palla in Faridabad, died after the car he was fleeing police in collided head-on with an oncoming truck near Goyla village and Dhulawat on the Kundli-Manesar-Palwal (KMP) Expressway in Nuh. The incident occurred between 5:30am and 6am on Wednesday; Mustafa had two criminal cases against him, including cattle smuggling and attacking police personnel. Three other occupants—Mohammad Akhlaq, Asif (both from Palla), and Mohammad Iqbal of Mankaki in Palwal—were injured and rushed to hospitals while the car sped toward Manesar on the wrong side of the expressway after police spotted them unloading a cow at Dhulawat. One smuggled cattle animal also died in the crash, though its companion survived. Police registered an FIR against the suspects under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Haryana Gauvansh Sanrakshan and Gau Samvardhan Act.
items.title: Suspected Cattle Smuggler Killed After Car Collides With Truck on KMP Expressway in Nuh

items.summary: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced on Nov. 19 a government order recognizing the permanent right of the Mẽbêngôkre (Kayapó) and Yudjá (Juruna) peoples over the 362,000-hectare (895,000-acre) Kapôt Nhĩnore Indigenous Territory in southern Brazil's Amazon. The two groups have fought for legal rights to the land since 2004, and Lula signed the ordinance during a ceremony following his visit to Chief Raoni Metuktire, who was born on the territory where his father is buried. Full legal recognition still requires borders marked on the ground, final presidential decree approval, and official registration before authorities can remove non-Indigenous occupants.
items.title: Brazil's President Lula Moves to Recognize Chief Raoni's Indigenous Land

items.summary: The article argues that UK energy bills are set to rise rather than fall over the next several years. Average annual energy bills reached £2,166 for Q1 2027 (q1), and Ofgem may cap prices at £2,000-plus in every quarter of 2027 (q2). A Wednesday announcement raised the price cap by £443, with gas identified as the overwhelming cause — though those prices could fall if calm returns to the Strait of Hormuz. EDF's outlook shows bills rising further: £2,254 for Q2 (which includes about £100 in network costs tied to grid upgrades), then £2,078 from July and £2,035 from October (q5–q8). The author contends that no one — certainly not government ministers — can claim surprise at a prolonged crisis. Two policy points follow: the government should stop ad hoc handouts like this quarter's £100 council tax rebate for lower bands (an inadequate proxy for hardship) and instead enact a properly targeted social tariff, with next winter as a hard deadline; and its goal to bring UK energy costs in line with European averages within 10 years is more credible than Keir Starmer's
items.title: UK Energy Bills May Rise to £2,000+ in Every Quarter of 2027

items.summary: President Donald Trump announced a series of new tariffs spanning 14 countries or trading partners, raising the tariff on Chinese products from about 20% to about 40%, and setting the EU tariff at 15%, which equals the maximum rate agreed in a 2025 US–EU negotiation. In addition to China and the EU, Trump added tariffs on Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam. The administration cited section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 as the legal basis for these measures; though no timeline was given by the White House, the tariffs could take effect in January at the earliest, with a US trade office investigation hearing scheduled for 25 January.
items.title: Trump Announces New Tariffs on 14 Trading Partners

items.summary: Enserva, the Canadian Energy Services Association trade group, warned in its 2026-27 State of the Industry Report that labor shortages—alongside inflationary cost pressures, U.S. trade relations, and potential Middle East-driven demand destruction—are key constraints on Canada's oil and gas sector growth, even as overall prospects turn positive for the first time in years. The report attributes this optimism to higher prices, supportive fiscal and regulatory policy, a federally designated 1-million-barrels-per-day West Coast pipeline project of national interest (proposed by Alberta to reduce dependence on U.S. exports), expanding LNG facilities including Woodfibre, Cedar, Ksi Lisims, and LNG Canada, oil sands growth, and data center demand for gas. Drilling activity is projected to rise 2% this year and 4% in 2027; natural gas drilling should rebound with a 7% increase in 2027 after two years of lower activity (following declines in 2025 and 2026); oil sands drilling will be flat in 2026 then rise 2% in 2027, up from a 2% decline in 2025; and conventional oil drilling should rebound 3% in 2026 after a 13% slump in 2025, expanding another 4% in 2027 amid higher prices linked to the U.S.-Iran conflict. However, Enserva cautioned that employment has dropped in Alberta and British Columbia over the past year—Saskatchewan being the only province with growth since September 2025—and Energy Safety Canada forecasts labor shortages as early as 2027 because emerging industries like infrastructure construction, AI, and data centers compete for the same skilled workforce. Enserva President Gurpreet Lail said
items.title: Labor Shortages Threaten Canada's Oil and Gas Growth Momentum

items.summary: On Nov. 24, around 40 community representatives gathered in Lamu to virtually witness an Environment and Land Court hearing challenging the East Africa Petroleum Refinery project of Nigeria's Dangote group, owned by billionaire Aliko Dangote. The refinery is estimated at $16 billion with a reported capacity of 700,000 barrels per day, which would make it the largest in Africa if built. Residents say they were not informed beforehand and lack formal land title deeds, prompting the government to ask them to leave; elder Mzee Hilal Suleiman Ali told Mongabay that although they are not opposed to the project, they want information, inclusion, and to keep their land. The hearing took place at the court in Malindi, about 200 kilometers (125 miles) from Lamu along Kenya's coast; because attending in person was too costly, residents watched remotely via phone while their lawyer participated virtually. After several hours, Judge Jane Onyango adjourned on procedural grounds until Dec. 15, requiring the plaintiffs to submit the emailed complaint in person in Nairobi with copies for all parties before it can proceed. Residents expressed frustration that they felt the process was being delayed and discouraged, though plaintiffs' lawyer George Wakahiu remained optimistic after learning the National Land Commission is now coming to the ground.
items.title: Kenyan Communities Challenge Dangote's $16 Billion Refinery as Court Adjourns Hearing

items.summary: South Africa is moving forward with plans to install 5.2 gigawatts (GW) of new nuclear capacity, which Energy Minister Kgosientsho Ramokgopa said Eskom has submitted a feasibility report for and welcomed as procurement of the same amount. The planned units would supplement South Africa's two existing reactors at Koeberg near Cape Town, whose combined 1.85 GW capacity entered commercial service in 1984 and 1985 and generates about 5% of the country's electricity today. Under Eskom's feasibility report for this extra capacity, the new nuclear generation is scheduled to come on stream by 2039 under South Africa's Integrated Resource Plan (IRP), which Energy Minister Ramokgopa said calls for more than 105 GWe of new generation capacity by that year through expansion of solar PV, wind and nuclear. The proposed small modular reactors would help replace retiring coal units—coal-fired stations near Mpumalanga supply roughly three-quarters of the country's power—and diversify supply away from aging, emissions-heavy plants; IRP frameworks also account for industrial demand such as mines buying power directly or building behind-the-meter hybrid systems. NESCA said it launched an Expression of Interest to identify technology partners and could pursue the Pebble Bed Modular Reactor program, which was moved out of care and maintenance last year.
items.title: South Africa Plans to Add 5.2 GW of Nuclear Capacity via Small Modular Reactors

items.summary: ChargePoint has partnered with German snow-groomer maker Kässbohrer (maker of the PistenBully brand) to supply charging for ski resorts and indoor ski facilities across Europe and North America. Under the agreement, Kässbohrer will connect its customers with ChargePoint for chargers plus software and support covering planning, installation, and day-to-day operations; a resort can use the same provider both for grooming vehicles at the maintenance depot and for EV chargers skiers use on the slopes. The deal centers on Kässbohrer's first fully electric groomer, the PistenBully 100 E, which according to the manufacturer has a 196 kWh battery that supports up to three hours of normal grooming per charge, accepts up to 22 kW on AC or 150 kW on a DC fast charger, and charges from zero to 100% in about an hour. ChargePoint says Kässbohrer accounts for more than half of the snow groomers sold worldwide each year, but which resorts will install chargers first and how many are still to be determined.
items.title: ChargePoint Partners With PistenBully Maker Kässbohrer to Bring EV Charging to Ski Resorts

items.summary: MEPs Marcos Ros (S&D) and Ondřej Kolář (EPP) debated the future of the EU budget on The Ring in Strasbourg, examining whether a deal is in sight. The European Commission has proposed a new €45 billion loan to Ukraine as it faces Russia's war, with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz tying approval of that same €45 billion loan for Kyiv to agreeing to broader EU budget terms. The debate centers on how the money will be financed and who ultimately bears the cost, raising questions about European solidarity and financial responsibility. Lawmakers are also weighing whether Ukraine aid can continue without cutting funds from other areas such as the EU's cohesion policy.
items.title: EU Budget Debate Over Ukraine Loan and Other Priorities

items.summary: On November 18, model and entrepreneur Hailey Bieber appeared at the DealBook Summit for a roughly 20-minute interview with Andrew Ross Sorkin about her beauty brand Rhode. The event drew attention partly because she wore a black wool-blend Yohji Yamamoto jacket from the Spring/Summer 1998 collection — the same design Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy had worn in June 1998 alongside John F. Kennedy Jr., and an identical piece later sold on The RealReal for $7,025 before the summit; her stylist confirmed it came from Tab Vintage. Sorkin introduced Bieber as a cultural force who shapes both culture and the economy, noting that she launched Rhode in 2022 and that e.l.f. Beauty acquired it less than three years later in a deal worth up to $1 billion. The interview became controversial after Sorkin asked whether Bieber had imagined such a valuation and then questioned what gave her confidence to believe she could achieve it, prompting widespread social media commentary about the perceived misogyny of the questioning and claims that she appeared ill-prepared on business management — though Business of Fashion also noted some criticism was justified. The article frames this as an unusual case in which both the alleged bias against Bieber and accusations of her incompetence became mainstream talking points.
items.title: DealBook Interview With Hailey Bieber Sparked Debate Over Questioning of Her Business Credentials

items.summary: Prime Minister Peter Magyar opened his first visit to Ukraine with a symbolic ceremony in the Transcarpathian city of Uzhhorod, where he laid flowers and bowed before an ethnic Hungarian soldier killed early in Russia's full-scale invasion. The gesture underscored Hungary's shift from Viktor Orban's pro-Russian stance—under which relations hit a historic low—to what both leaders called a
items.title: Hungary and Ukraine Reset Relations at Uzhhorod Cemetery Meeting

items.summary: A study on AI's role in research found that recent frontier models now consistently propose research designs judged as more compelling than those developed by the top expert in a given field. This assessment held across both human graders and large language model (LLM) graders. However, despite these high-quality designs, they frequently serve new research questions that graders rated as substantially less valuable than leading work in political science.
items.title: AI Research Designs Now Outperform Expert Work, Though Their Topics Remain Less Valuable

items.summary: Mozambique secured their place in the Round of 32 at the FIFA Under-17 World Cup in Qatar by drawing 2-2 with Australia in Group C, which guaranteed their progression from the group stage. The team had also faced Denmark and Argentina during the tournament. Their coach described reaching this point as a victory for Mozambique, noting that the players worked very hard throughout the campaign, though he acknowledged they could not handle losing to a 2-0 deficit.
items.title: Mozambique Advance to Round of 32 After Drawing 2-2 With Australia

items.summary: Kilmar Abrego García, a Salvadoran man at the centre of controversy over President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown, arrived in Madrid on Wednesday after voluntarily leaving the United States and concluding 20 months of litigation. His lawyers described the move as temporary; he is married to a US citizen and hopes to return once Trump leaves office. Abrego García was arrested in March 2025 and deported despite a court order prohibiting his removal, landing in El Salvador's Terrorism Confinement Centre (CECOT), where he reported beatings, sleep deprivation, and psychological torture during nearly three months of detention. The US government later acknowledged the deportation had been
items.title: Wrongly Deported Salvadoran Arrives in Spain After US Legal Battle

items.summary: A Polish deputy defence minister announced Wednesday that Poland will soon establish a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border, following repeated airspace incursions it attributes to Russia. The move comes as Poland continues to support Ukraine in its fight against what it describes as Moscow's nearly five-year invasion and has repeatedly accused Russia of attempting to target Kyiv's allies through drone incursions and other methods. According to FRANCE 24 reporter Selina Sykes, the no-fly zone is designed to enable Polish forces to quickly identify any Russian military aircraft and shoot them down if necessary.
items.title: Poland Plans No-Fly Zone at Ukraine Border After Airspace Violations
